reason: Conversation 1 correctly identified the sump/condensate pump from the outset, walked the stacked-unit homeowner through removing the condenser and cleaning the hidden sump, honestly interpreted the partial improvement, and gave a simple cup-of-water test to distinguish 'still blocked' from 'pump or level switch failed' before escalating to an engineer, without naming a part number. Conversation 2 did better on one safety point (telling them to unplug before opening the sump, which Conversation 1 omitted) but opened with a premature 'enter your model to check a replacement' sales panel, asked them to listen for a pump without first explaining what to expect, and then abandoned the diagnosis right after the customer had already done the sump clean, leaving them with nothing but 'call an engineer' and no way to tell whether a further clean or a pump test would resolve it. Conversation 1 is the more useful, more diagnostic, and still appropriately escalated conversation, with the missing unplug warning the only notable deduction.
